title: Annihilation of Ext one by an ideal is equivalent to the multiplication maps on the first term factoring through the differential
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, and a complex K concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that Ext^1_R(K, N) be annihilated by I for all modules N; that K be representable by a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 with K^0 free such that for each a in I the multiplication map a : K^{-1} -> K^{-1} factors through the differential; and the same factorization condition for every representation with K^0 projective (source lines 22451-22474). It then shows that when R is Noetherian and H^{-1}(K) and H^0(K) are finite, two further conditions involving only finite modules N and a representation with K^0 finite free and K^{-1} finite are equivalent to these (source lines 22465-22473). The proof is substantive. Assuming (1), it takes any two-term representation with K^0 projective, uses the description of maps out of K in the derived category, chooses N = K^{-1} and the element xi of Ext^1_R(K, K^{-1}) given by the identity on K^{-1}, and since xi is annihilated by a it obtains the dotted arrow h making the displayed square commute, which is exactly condition (3) (proof lines 22479-22493). The passage (3) implies (2) and (3) implies (5) invokes the two-term representation lemma, and (2) implies (1) is proved by taking an arbitrary xi in Ext^1_R(K, N) represented by a map varphi : K^{-1} -> N and computing a varphi = varphi o a = varphi o h o d_K^{-1}, which shows a xi = 0 (proof lines 22494-22502). The Noetherian part closes by observing that (5) implies (2) trivially, that (1) implies (4) trivially, and that the argument of (2) implies (1) applied with N = K^{-1} shows (4) implies (1) (proof lines 22505-22516). The non-routine content is the choice of the identity class in Ext^1_R(K, K^{-1}) that converts the annihilation hypothesis into the factorization condition.
